## Access

One CSV (100,842 records, 14 MiB) from GFZ Data Services, downloaded once by `craton bench prepare`, checked against the release's sha256 and cached.

## What is used

| | |
|---|---|
| `used by` | CB-23 only, as the answer; no model or floor reads it as input |
| `azimuth` | `AZI`: SHmax, degrees east of north, axial (0 = 180) |
| `quality` | `QUALITY` A, B or C only (1σ 15°, 20°, 25°) |
| `depth` | `DEPTH` (km); records deeper than 40 km are left out |
| `kind` | `TYPE`: FMS single focal mechanism, FMF formal inversion, BO borehole breakouts, HF hydraulic fracturing, GFI fault-slip, … |

## Uncertainty

Each record's quality stands for a 1σ of its azimuth: A ±15°, B ±20°, C ±25°. A single focal mechanism (most records) gives the stress axes only within the angle between its P axis and the true σ1, which is why WSM rates it C at best.

## Known issues

- 85% of the records are single focal mechanisms, from the same quakes Craton reads as positions, times and magnitudes. A method sees where quakes were, never how they slipped, so the mechanism is still unseen data.
- Coverage follows seismicity and drilling: dense in Japan and California, a few hundred records in Alaska or central Italy.
- Records within one cell can disagree by more than their quality allows where the stress turns over a few km (a fault bend, a volcano, a slab).
